in.why: Say a before a job word.
in.answer_say: A teacher! He is a teacher.

native.hook: 「I am student」で止まってない？
native.tip: 職業の前には a が必要。日本語にない「a」を忘れずに！
native.caption: “I am student.”と言っていませんか？😅 日本語には冠詞がないので、つい抜けがち。職業の前には a をつけます。 “I am a student.” が自然な言い方です。Amaの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“a”。a を入れて自然な英語に。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: Put a before a job word. It is easy to forget!
en.caption: Do you say this? “I am student.” 😅 The little word a often goes missing. Put a before a job. The natural way is “I am a student.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Child has a special plural: children.
in.answer_say: Children! I have three children.

native.hook: two child、複数形が抜けてない？
native.tip: 2つ以上なら複数形。child の複数形は children（childs ではない）。
native.caption: “I have two child.”と言っていませんか？😅 数が2以上のときは名詞を複数形にします。child は特別で children になります。 “I have two children.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“children”。child の複数形は children。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.hook: Two child? Is the plural missing?
en.tip: With two or more, use the plural. Child becomes children.
en.caption: Do you say this? “I have two child.” 😅 With two or more, the noun must be plural. Child is special: children. The natural way is “I have two children.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: With yesterday, use the simple past.
in.answer_say: Saw! I saw him yesterday.

native.hook: yesterday と have seen？注意！
native.tip: 「昨日」など過去の時を言うなら、過去形 saw を使います。
native.caption: “I have seen him yesterday.”と言っていませんか？😅 yesterday のように過去の時がはっきりしているときは、現在完了ではなく過去形を使います。 “I saw him yesterday.” が自然な言い方です。Amaの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“saw”。yesterday には過去形。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: With a clear past time like yesterday, use the simple past.
en.caption: Do you say this? “I have seen him yesterday.” 😅 With a clear past time such as yesterday, use the simple past, not the present perfect. The natural way is “I saw him yesterday.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Arrive goes with at, not to.
in.answer_say: At! I arrived at the station.

native.hook: 「到着する」に to を使ってない？
native.tip: arrive の後は場所なら at、都市なら in を使います。to は使いません。
native.caption: “I arrived to the station.”と言っていませんか？😅 日本語の「に」につられて to を使いがち。arrive の後は at を使います。 “I arrived at the station.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“at”。arrive のあとは at か in。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: After arrive, use at for places or in for cities. Not to.
en.caption: Do you say this? “I arrived to the station.” 😅 It is easy to use to, but after arrive you say at. The natural way is “I arrived at the station.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: A mansion is a very big house.

quiz.stem: I rent a small ___ near the station.

in.answer_say: Apartment! I rent a small apartment.

native.hook: 「マンション」は英語で通じない
native.tip: 英語の mansion は大豪邸。日本のマンションは apartment と言います。
native.caption: “My mansion is small.”と言っていませんか？😅 英語の mansion は「大豪邸」のこと。日本でいうマンションは apartment（または condo）です。 “My apartment is small.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“apartment”。mansion は大豪邸のこと。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.hook: Is your home really a mansion?
en.tip: A mansion is a huge house. A normal home in a building is an apartment.
en.caption: Do you say this? “My mansion is small.” 😅 In English a mansion is a huge house. A normal home in a building is an apartment. The natural way is “My apartment is small.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Say excited, not high tension.
in.answer_say: Excited! I am excited about the trip.

native.hook: 「ハイテンション」は和製英語
native.tip: tension は「緊張」の意味。盛り上がっているなら excited を使おう。
native.caption: “I am high tension today.”と言っていませんか？😅 日本語の「ハイテンション」は和製英語です。英語の tension は緊張や不安のこと。元気なら excited と言います。 “I am so excited today.” が自然な言い方です。Amaの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“excited”。ハイテンションは和製英語。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: Tension means stress. When you feel full of energy, say excited.
en.caption: Do you say this? “I am high tension today.” 😅 In English, tension means stress. When you feel full of energy, say excited. The natural way is “I am so excited today.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: We make a mistake, not do.
in.answer_say: Made! I made a mistake.

native.hook: mistake は do じゃなくて make
native.tip: 「間違える」は make a mistake。do は使いません。セットで覚えよう。
native.caption: “I did a mistake.”と言っていませんか？😅 「間違いをする」を do で訳したくなりますが、英語では make a mistake がセットの言い方です。 “I made a mistake.” が自然な言い方です。Amaの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“made”。make a mistake で一つの表現。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.hook: Is it “do” a mistake? Not really!
en.tip: Say make a mistake. Learn the two words together.
en.caption: Do you say this? “I did a mistake.” 😅 Do feels right, but English says make a mistake as a set phrase. The natural way is “I made a mistake.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Say on foot for walking.
in.answer_say: On! I go to school on foot.

native.hook: 「歩いて」は by walk じゃない
native.tip: 乗り物は by、歩きは on foot。決まったセットで言います。
native.caption: “I go there by walk.”と言っていませんか？😅 電車は by train なので、歩きも by walk と言いたくなります。でも歩きは on foot が決まり文句です。 “I go there on foot.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“on”。歩きは on foot。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: For vehicles use by. For walking, say on foot.
en.caption: Do you say this? “I go there by walk.” 😅 By train works, so by walk feels logical. But for walking the set phrase is on foot. The natural way is “I go there on foot.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Agree is a verb. No am.
in.answer_say: Agree! I agree with you.

native.hook: 「I am agree」になってない？
native.tip: agree は動詞なので be 動詞はいりません。I agree でOK！
native.caption: “I am agree.”と言っていませんか？😅 日本語の「賛成だ」につられて am を入れがち。agree はそれだけで動詞なので、I agree と言います。 “I agree.” が自然な言い方です。Amaの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“agree”。be 動詞は不要です。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: Agree is already a verb, so no am is needed. Just say I agree.
en.caption: Do you say this? “I am agree.” 😅 It is easy to add am, but agree is a verb by itself. The natural way is “I agree.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: We take medicine. We do not drink it.
in.answer_say: Take! I take medicine every day.

native.hook: 薬を「飲む」は drink じゃない
native.tip: 薬は「飲む」でも take を使います。drink は使いません。
native.caption: “I drank medicine.”と言っていませんか？😅 「薬を飲む」をそのまま drink と訳しがちですが、英語では take medicine と言います。“I took medicine.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“take”。薬は take。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: Use take for medicine, not drink.
en.caption: Do you say this? “I drank medicine.” 😅 English says take medicine. The natural way is “I took medicine.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I am difficult to get up early.
in.right: It is hard for me to get up early.
in.why: Start with It: it is hard for me to...
in.memory: It is hard for me to get up early.

quiz.stem: ___ is hard for me to wake up.

in.answer_say: It! It is hard for me to wake up.

native.hook: 「私は難しい」になってない？
native.tip: 「私は〜するのが難しい」は I am difficult ではなく It is hard for me to ~ の形で。
native.caption: “I am difficult to get up early.”と言っていませんか？😅 「私は早起きが難しい」と主語を I にすると不自然に。difficult は物事に使うので、It を主語にします。 “It is hard for me to get up early.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“It”。It is hard for me to ～ の形を使おう。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: For things that are hard for you, start with It is hard for me to...
en.caption: Do you say this? “I am difficult to get up early.” 😅 Making I the subject sounds odd here. Start with It. The natural way is “It is hard for me to get up early.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: People is plural. Use are.
in.answer_say: Are! Many people are here.

native.hook: people は単数？複数？
native.tip: people は複数扱い。is ではなく are を使います。
native.caption: “People is very kind here.”と言っていませんか？😅 日本語では人数に関係なく同じ形ですが、英語の people は複数扱い。動詞は are になります。 “People are very kind here.” が自然な言い方です。Amaの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“are”。people は複数扱い。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: People is plural. Use are, not is.
en.caption: Do you say this? “People is very kind here.” 😅 People is plural, so the verb is are. The natural way is “People are very kind here.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.right: I have a lot of homework.
in.why: Homework has no plural.
in.memory: I have a lot of homework.
in.answer_say: Homework! I have too much homework.

native.hook: homework に s をつけてない？
native.tip: homework は数えられない名詞。s は付けず、a lot of で量を表します。
native.caption: “I have many homeworks.”と言っていませんか？😅 homework は数えられない名詞なので、s は付けません。たくさんは many ではなく a lot of を使います。 “I have a lot of homework.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“homework”。数えられない名詞に s は不要。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.hook: Do you add s to homework?
en.tip: Homework cannot be counted. No s. Say a lot of homework.
en.caption: Do you say this? “I have many homeworks.” 😅 Homework is uncountable, so no s. For a large amount, use a lot of. The natural way is “I have a lot of homework.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Past time needs a past verb.
in.answer_say: Ate! Yesterday I ate rice.

native.hook: 過去の話なのに eat のまま？
native.tip: 昨日の話なら、英語は動詞を過去形に。eat → ate！
native.caption: “I eat natto yesterday.”と言っていませんか？😅 yesterday があっても、英語では動詞そのものを過去形にします。eat の過去形は ate。“I ate natto yesterday.” が自然な言い方です。Amaの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“ate”。昨日の話は過去形。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: English changes the verb for the past: eat becomes ate.
en.caption: Do you say this? “I eat natto yesterday.” 😅 Yesterday is not enough. The verb itself must change: eat becomes ate. The natural way is “I ate natto yesterday.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Time here has no a.
in.answer_say: Time! Sorry, I don't have time today.

native.hook: 「時間がない」に a は不要
native.tip: 「時間」の意味の time は数えられない名詞。a は付けません。
native.caption: “I don't have a time.”と言っていませんか？😅 「時間」という意味の time は数えられない名詞です。a は付けず、I don't have time と言います。 “I don't have time.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“time”。時間の time に a は不要。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.hook: Do you say “I don't have a time”?
en.tip: Time meaning free time has no a. Say I don't have time.
en.caption: Do you say this? “I don't have a time.” 😅 Time as free time is uncountable, so no a. The natural way is “I don't have time.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.hook_say: In a taxi, on a train!
in.why: Small cars use in. Big ones use on.
in.answer_say: In! I got in the taxi.

native.hook: タクシーに「on」で乗ってない？
native.tip: 車・タクシーは in、電車・バスは on。乗り物の大きさで使い分けます。
native.caption: “I got on the taxi.”と言っていませんか？😅 車やタクシーのような小さい乗り物は in、電車やバスのような大きい乗り物は on を使います。 “I got in the taxi.” が自然な言い方です。Amaの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“in”。車は in、電車は on。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: Use in for cars and taxis. Use on for trains and buses.
en.caption: Do you say this? “I got on the taxi.” 😅 Small vehicles like cars and taxis use in. Big ones like trains and buses use on. The natural way is “I got in the taxi.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.hook_say: Very much goes at the end!
in.why: Put very much after the thing.
in.answer_say: I like cats very much!

native.hook: 「とても好き」は very like？
native.tip: very は動詞の前に置けません。like ～ very much の順にします。
native.caption: “I very like pizza.”と言っていませんか？😅 「とても好き」を I very like と言いたくなりますが、英語では very much を文の後ろに置きます。 “I like pizza very much.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“I like cats very much.” very much は後ろに置きます。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: Very cannot go before a verb. Say like it very much.
en.caption: Do you say this? “I very like pizza.” 😅 English puts very much after the object. The natural way is “I like pizza very much.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.right: I listen to music every day.
in.why: Listen needs to before the thing.
in.memory: I listen to music every day.
in.answer_say: To! I listen to music.

native.hook: 「音楽を聞く」で to が消えてる
native.tip: listen は「listen to ～」の形。to を忘れずに！
native.caption: “I listen music every day.”と言っていませんか？😅 日本語の「音楽を聞く」には「を」しかないので、to が抜けがち。listen のあとは to が必要です。 “I listen to music every day.” が自然な言い方です。Amaの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“to”。listen のあとは to。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: Listen always needs to before the thing you hear.
en.caption: Do you say this? “I listen music every day.” 😅 It is easy to drop to, but English needs listen to. The natural way is “I listen to music every day.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: After can, use the plain verb.
in.answer_say: Speak! I can speak English.

native.hook: can のあとに to を入れてない？
native.tip: can のあとは動詞の原形だけ。to はいりません。
native.caption: “She can to speak English.”と言っていませんか？😅 can のような助動詞のあとには、to なしの動詞の原形が続きます。be able to と混ざらないように。 “She can speak English.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“speak”。can のあとは原形。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: After can, use the plain verb. No to.
en.caption: Do you say this? “She can to speak English.” 😅 After a modal like can, the base verb follows without to. Do not mix it with be able to. The natural way is “She can speak English.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: After doesn't, the verb has no s.
in.answer_say: Like! She doesn't like it.

native.hook: doesn't のあとに s をつけてない？
native.tip: doesn't がすでに三単現の s を持っているので、動詞は原形に。
native.caption: “He doesn't likes it.”と言っていませんか？😅 否定文では doesn't が三人称単数を担当します。そのため like は s のない原形になります。 “He doesn't like it.” が自然な言い方です。Amaの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“like”。doesn't のあとは原形。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.hook: Do you add s after doesn't?
en.tip: Doesn't already carries the s. Use the plain verb: like.
en.caption: Do you say this? “He doesn't likes it.” 😅 In negatives, doesn't handles the third person, so the verb stays plain. The natural way is “He doesn't like it.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: If you don't, say no.

quiz.stem: You don't like fish? ___, I don't.

in.answer_say: No! No, I don't.

native.hook: Yes か No か？日本人の癖の罠！
native.tip: 英語では事実で答えます。否定なら No と言います。
native.caption: “Yes, I don't like fish.”と言っていませんか？😅 日本語は相手の言葉に同意するかで「はい」と答えますが、英語は答えの内容が否定なら No です。 “No, I don't like fish.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“No”。否定の答えは No。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.hook: Yes or No? Watch this trap!
en.tip: In English, answer by the fact. If it is negative, say No.
en.caption: Do you say this? “Yes, I don't like fish.” 😅 In English, answer by the fact. If your answer is negative, say No. The natural way is “No, I don't like fish.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Use a full phrase: I'm late.
in.answer_say: Late! Sorry, I'm late.

native.hook: 「遅れてごめん」の言い方は？
native.tip: Sorry for late は不自然。Sorry I'm late. と主語と動詞を入れます。
native.caption: “Sorry for late.”と言っていませんか？😅 日本語の「遅れてごめん」をそのまま訳すと不自然に。Sorry のあとは I'm late と文の形にします。 “Sorry I'm late.” が自然な言い方です。Amaの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“late”。I'm late と文で言おう。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: Say Sorry I'm late. Use a full sentence after sorry.
en.caption: Do you say this? “Sorry for late.” 😅 A word-for-word translation sounds odd. After sorry, say a full phrase: I'm late. The natural way is “Sorry I'm late.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Wait needs for before the thing.
in.answer_say: For! I am waiting for my friend.

native.hook: 「I waited the bus」で合ってる？
native.tip: wait のあとには for が必要。「バスを待つ」につられて忘れがち。
native.caption: “I waited the bus.”と言っていませんか？😅 日本語の「バスを待った」につられて、for を抜かしがちです。wait のあとには for が必要です。 “I waited for the bus.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“for”。wait のあとは for。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.hook: Do you say “I waited the bus”?
en.tip: Wait needs for before the thing you wait for.
en.caption: Do you say this? “I waited the bus.” 😅 It is easy to drop for, but wait needs it. The natural way is “I waited for the bus.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Discuss already means talk about.
in.answer_say: Discussed! We discussed the trip.

native.hook: 「discuss about」の about は不要
native.tip: discuss は「〜について話し合う」の意味を含む。about は付けない。
native.caption: “Let's discuss about the plan.”と言っていませんか？😅 日本語の「〜について」につられて about を付けがちです。discuss だけで「〜について話し合う」になります。 “Let's discuss the plan.” が自然な言い方です。Amaの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“discussed”。discuss のあとに about は不要。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: Discuss already means talk about. Do not add about.
en.caption: Do you say this? “Let's discuss about the plan.” 😅 It is easy to add about, but discuss already includes it. The natural way is “Let's discuss the plan.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Do not drop the subject.
in.answer_say: I went to Kyoto!

native.hook: 「Went to Kyoto」、「I」を忘れてない？
native.tip: 日本語は主語を省くのが普通。でも英語では I を省かずに言おう。
native.caption: “Went to Kyoto yesterday.”と言っていませんか？😅 日本語では「京都に行った」で通じますが、英語では主語の I が必要です。“I went to Kyoto yesterday.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“I went to Kyoto yesterday.” 主語の I を忘れずに。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: Do not drop the subject. Say I went...
en.caption: Do you say this? “Went to Kyoto yesterday.” 😅 English needs the subject I. The natural way is “I went to Kyoto yesterday.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I look forward to see you.

in.why: After this to, say seeing, not see.

native.hook: look forward to の後ろ、動詞の形は大丈夫？
native.tip: look forward to の to は前置詞。だから後ろは seeing のように -ing 形。
native.caption: “I look forward to see you.”と言っていませんか？😅 「to の後ろは原形」と覚えていて原形にしがちですが、この to は前置詞なので -ing 形が正解。“I look forward to seeing you.” が自然な言い方です。Amaの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“watching”。look forward to の後ろは -ing 形。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.hook: Look forward to see, or seeing?
en.tip: The to here is a preposition, so use the ing form.
en.caption: Do you say this? “I look forward to see you.” 😅 The to in this phrase is a preposition, so the verb takes ing. The natural way is “I look forward to seeing you.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

quiz.stem: There is no ___ by my desk.

in.answer_say: Outlet! There is no outlet by my desk.

native.hook: 「コンセント」は英語じゃない！通じないかも
native.tip: 日本語の「コンセント」は和製英語。壁の差し込み口は outlet と言う。
native.caption: “My room has no consent.”と言っていませんか？😅 「コンセント」は和製英語です。英語の consent は「同意」の意味になってしまいます。壁の差し込み口は outlet。“My room has no outlet.” が自然な言い方です。Amaの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。

en.tip: Consent means permission. A wall socket is an outlet.

in.why: There already means to there.

native.tip: there は「そこへ」の意味を持つ。to はつけずに went there と言う。
native.caption: “I went to there yesterday.”と言っていませんか？😅 日本語の「そこに行く」につられて to を入れがちですが、there だけで「そこへ」の意味になります。“I went there yesterday.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“there”。there に to は不要。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: There already means to that place, so drop to.

in.wrong: I study English since last year.
in.right: I have studied English since last year.
in.why: Since needs the present perfect, not the present.
in.memory: I have studied English since last year.
in.answer_say: Have lived! I have lived here since May.

native.hook: 「since」の文、動詞の形は合ってる？
native.tip: since を使うときは現在完了形（have + 過去分詞）。日本語の「勉強している」につられないで。
native.caption: “I study English since last year.”と言っていませんか？😅 日本語の「去年から勉強している」につられて現在形にしがちですが、since には現在完了形を使います。“I have studied English since last year.” が自然な言い方です。Amaの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“have lived”。since には have + 過去分詞。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: Use the present perfect with since, not the present.
en.caption: Do you say this? “I study English since last year.” 😅 With since, English needs the present perfect. The natural way is “I have studied English since last year.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: He is a friend of me.
in.right: He is a friend of mine.
in.why: In “a friend of ___,” use mine, not me.

native.hook: 「a friend of me」、me じゃなくて…？
native.tip: 「私の友達の一人」は a friend of mine。この形では of の後ろは me ではなく mine。

native.comment: 答え：“mine”。a friend of mine が正しい形。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: In this phrase, say a friend of mine, not of me.
en.caption: Do you say this? “He is a friend of me.” 😅 Say mine, not me, after of. The natural way is “He is a friend of mine.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
